svg.title: Escalation to War (1964–67): Water Politics, Fatah Raids, Samu & The 7 April 1967 Air Clash
svg.desc: Edexcel GCSE History Option P5 cartographic map illustrating Israel's 1964 National Water Carrier from Lake Kinneret to the Negev, Arab League headwater diversion works at Banias, Dan, and Hasbani, Syrian Golan artillery and Fatah guerrilla raids, Israel's 13 November 1966 daylight reprisal at Samu in the Jordanian West Bank, and the 7 April 1967 aerial dogfight downing six Syrian MiG-21s near Damascus.

g.text: Arab League plan (1964) to divert Jordan sources;
IDF tanks & jets bomb Syrian canal works (1965–66).
Radical 1966 Syrian regime backs Arafat's Fatah raids;
Golan guns shell Galilee kibbutzim below the plateau.
Pipelines pump Sea of Galilee water to the Negev,
prompting Nasser's Jan 1964 Cairo Summit & PLO founding.
4,000 IDF troops & tanks strike Jordanian West Bank
after Fatah landmine: 15 Jordanian troops killed, 100+
homes flattened → West Bank riots shake King Hussein.
IAF Mirage jets shoot down 6 Syrian
EDEXCEL GCSE HISTORY • OPTION P5: ESCALATION TO WAR (1964–67)
Water Politics, Fatah Raids, Samu & The 7 April 1967 Air Clash
Causal Chain: Water clashes (1964–66) + Syrian-backed Fatah raids + Samu (Nov 1966) + 7 April 1967 air rout → Soviet false alarm to Cairo (May 1967).
